blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object is a Deployment for blue, the version running now. It comes from apps/v1.
blocks.why: Blue-green runs the new version, green, beside blue. Then one change moves all traffic.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create first: the blue Deployment

blocks.title: Name the blue copy
blocks.why: Each version gets its own Deployment, so both can run at once.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: The Deployment for the blue version
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue

blocks.title: Which Pods are blue?
blocks.what: The selector manages Pods labelled app: shop and version: blue.
blocks.why: Both versions share app: shop. The version label tells them apart.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Manage Pods that are shop and blue
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop
      version: blue

blocks.title: Describe the blue Pods
blocks.what: Each Pod gets both labels: app: shop and version: blue.
blocks.why: The Service looks for these labels to decide where traffic goes.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: Label each Pod as shop and blue
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop
      version: blue
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop
        version: blue

blocks.title: A page that says blue
blocks.what: busybox writes a page saying blue, then serves it on port 80.
blocks.why: Fetching the page shows which version answered.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: A small web server that answers blue
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop
      version: blue
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop
        version: blue
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo blue > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]

blocks.title: Add the Service
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a Service called shop.
blocks.why: Clients always use the name shop. They never need to know which version answers.
blocks.ifRemoved: Clients would have to find the blue Pods themselves.
blocks.comment: A second object: the Service clients use
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop
      version: blue
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop
        version: blue
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo blue > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: shop

blocks.title: Send traffic to blue
blocks.what: The selector sends traffic only to Pods that are shop and blue.
blocks.why: Changing version here from blue to green is the whole switch.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Service, because it must say which port to listen on.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop
      version: blue
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop
        version: blue
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo blue > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: shop
spec:
  selector:
    app: shop
    version: blue
  ports:
    - port: 80

blocks.title: Add the green copy
blocks.what: Three dashes start a third object: the Deployment for green, the new version.
blocks.why: Green starts beside blue and gets no traffic until the switch.
blocks.ifRemoved: There is no new version to switch to.
blocks.comment: A third object: the green Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-blue
spec:
  selector:

---
apiVersion: v1

metadata:

spec:
  selector:

apiVersion: apps/v1

metadata:
  name: shop-green

blocks.title: Which Pods are green?
blocks.what: The selector manages Pods labelled app: shop and version: green.
blocks.why: Same app, different version. The two Deployments never manage each other’s Pods.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Manage Pods that are shop and green

---

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version. Deployments are in apps/v1. Services are in the core v1 API.
notes.Deployment:kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.Service:kind: The type of object to create. A Service sends traffic to Pods with chosen labels.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Deployment:metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.Service:metadata.name: The Service name. Clients inside the cluster use http://shop.
notes.Deployment:spec: The desired state of this Deployment.
notes.Service:spec: The desired state: which Pods get traffic, on which port.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.Service:spec.selector: Pods must have all of these labels to receive traffic.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: The app label shared by both versions: shop.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod of both versions gets app: shop.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Write a page naming the version, then serve it on port 80 with busybox’s web server.
notes.spec.selector.app: Send traffic to Pods labelled app: shop.
notes.spec.ports: The ports the Service listens on. Each list item is one port.
notes.spec.ports[].port: Listen on port 80 and forward to port 80 on the Pods.
notes.spec.selector.version: Send traffic only to blue Pods. Change it to green to switch.

tryIt.result: Creates shop-blue, the shop Service, and shop-green.
Both versions show READY 1/1. Both run, but only one gets traffic.
Prints blue: the Service sends traffic to blue.
Changes the Service’s version label to green. In real work, edit the file and apply it.
Prints green. Every request now goes to green. Patch back to blue to undo.
Removes both Deployments and the Service.

questions.question: Which line decides whether blue or green gets the traffic?
questions.explain: The Service sends traffic to Pods with all its selector labels. Changing version moves every request.

questions.question: Green has a bug after the switch. What is the fastest way back?
answers: Change the Service selector back to blue
questions.explain: Blue is still running, so switching back is one change and takes effect at once.

questions.question: What is the cost of blue-green?
answers: Two full copies of the app run at the same time
questions.explain: Both versions run side by side, so you need room for both.

fix.message: The Deployment "shop-blue" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: {"matchLabels":{"app":"shop","version":"green"}}: field is immutable
fix.explain: The green copy kept blue’s name, a copy-paste slip. Kubernetes tries to turn shop-blue into green, and a selector cannot change.
fix.fix: Give the green Deployment its own name: shop-green.
